canonical_statement: Evo-Bench was designed to evaluate a language model's intrinsic ability to autonomously improve an executable agent harness under long-horizon iterative research.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: benchmark designed to evaluate models’ intrinsic harness-evolving capabilities

canonical_statement: The benchmark construction aims to isolate harness improvement from base-model strength, reduce task-specific overfitting, and measure long-horizon iterative evolution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: isolate harness improvements from base model strength

canonical_statement: Evo-Bench contains 608 tasks across Search, Office, and General agent domains.
The visible validation suite contains 160 tasks and the disjoint held-out evaluation suite contains 448 tasks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 160-task visible validation suite Dval and a disjoint 448-task evaluation suite

canonical_statement: Each source benchmark contributes 32 validation tasks; the evaluation split contains 128 BrowseComp, 128 HLE, 64 GDPval, 64 APEX-Agents, and 64 Claw-Eval tasks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each source benchmark contributes 32 validation tasks

canonical_statement: Each evolution run fixes a policy model and lets a separate evolver iteratively edit the policy harness using validation-side evidence before freezing the final revision for held-out evaluation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: final revision HT is frozen and evaluated on a disjoint held-out evaluation suite

canonical_statement: The policy harness starts from a minimal CodeAct loop with shell execution, while planning, memory, domain tools, and verification are left available for evolution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: minimal CodeAct loop with only a shell-execution tool

canonical_statement: Anytime Validation Score is the mean best-so-far validation score across the allowed evolution iterations, carrying the final best score forward after early termination.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: average best-so-far validation performance over the evolution budget

outcome.definition: Average of best-so-far validation performance across the evolution budget.

canonical_statement: Stage 1 selects auxiliary tasks with low average scores and longer interaction trajectories to create headroom and stronger signals for harness evolution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: select tasks with lower average scores and longer interaction trajectories

canonical_statement: Stage 1 produced a 320-task auxiliary set comprising 128 Search, 128 Office, and 64 General tasks.
Four frontier-model evolution runs produced 73 formally evaluated auxiliary harness variants.

concept.text: Auxiliary harness evolution with GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, and GPT-5.6-Sol

canonical_statement: A deterministic diversity-aware selection retained 12 representative auxiliary harnesses from the 73 evaluated variants.
Stage 2 evaluated 2,329 candidate tasks from five source benchmarks under the 12 selected auxiliary harnesses.
Harness sensitivity is computed as the Pearson correlation between a task's scores across auxiliary harnesses and the leave-one-task-out overall quality of those harnesses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: compute the Pearson correlation coefficient between task-level scores and overall harness quality

canonical_statement: Tasks with non-positive harness sensitivity are removed before sensitivity-aware stratified selection, and remaining tasks are stratified by difficulty to preserve difficulty diversity.
The appendix reports eight slightly negative-sensitivity Claw-Eval tasks were retained as quota backfills from sparse strata.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Eight slightly negative Claw-Eval tasks are quota backfills

canonical_statement: The CodeAct seed harness is the primary baseline used to quantify absolute gains from harness evolution.
The Artificial harness baseline is a composite of human-engineered domain-specific systems: MiroFlow for Search, Stirrup for Office, and Claw-Eval for General tasks.

exposures.details: MiroFlow for Search; Stirrup for Office; Claw-Eval for General

canonical_statement: Main experiments use DeepSeek-V4-Flash as the fixed policy model, a budget of 20 iterations, 1,000 evolver steps, and 48 hours, with one experimental run per evolver.
Search and Office tasks use one rollout per task, Claw-Eval uses three rollouts, and Qwen3.7-Plus is the common judge for tasks requiring LLM grading.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Search and office tasks use one rollout, whereas Claw-Eval use three rollouts

canonical_statement: The main leaderboard reports one evolution run per model rather than replicated independent runs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We run all experiments one time

canonical_statement: GPT-5.6 Sol achieved an Overall Score of 46.3, an absolute change of +16.6 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 50.1.
Claude Opus 4.8 achieved an Overall Score of 45.8, an absolute change of +16.1 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 51.4.
GLM-5.2 achieved an Overall Score of 43.5, an absolute change of +13.8 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 51.0.
Qwen3.7-Max achieved an Overall Score of 41.5, an absolute change of +11.8 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 49.3.
MiniMax M3 achieved an Overall Score of 41.4, an absolute change of +11.7 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 49.0.
Qwen3.6-27B achieved an Overall Score of 39.4, an absolute change of +9.7 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 46.9.
DeepSeek V4 Pro achieved an Overall Score of 39.1, an absolute change of +9.4 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 45.4.
Kimi K2.7 Code achieved an Overall Score of 38.7, an absolute change of +9.0 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 43.4.
Gemma 4 31B achieved an Overall Score of 35.9, an absolute change of +6.2 points from the CodeAct baseline, with AnytimeVal 36.2.
The best evolved harness, GPT-5.6 Sol at 46.3 Overall, remained 1.2 points below the Artificial harness composite at 47.5.
Claude Opus 4.8 achieved a Search score of 46.5, gaining 34.8 points over CodeAct and nearly matching the Artificial harness Search score of 46.7.
GPT-5.6 Sol achieved an Office score of 41.6 versus 38.4 for CodeAct and 43.9 for the Artificial harness.
Qwen3.7-Max slightly regressed on Office tasks, scoring 37.8 versus the CodeAct baseline of 38.4.
GPT-5.6 Sol scored 59.4 on General tasks, exceeding the Artificial harness score of 56.3 by 3.1 points.
Qwen3.7-Max also scored 59.4 on General tasks, exceeding the Artificial harness score of 56.3.

Harness-evolution gains were strongly domain-dependent: Search improved markedly, Office generally improved little or regressed, and top evolved harnesses surpassed the manual baseline on General tasks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: evolutionary gains are highly uneven across different task domains

canonical_statement: GPT-5.6 Sol used the full 20-iteration budget, 559 of 1,000 evolver steps, and 33.63 of 48 hours.
Qwen3.7-Max terminated after 15 iterations, 200 evolver steps, and 23.26 hours.
GPT-5.6 Sol incurred more than $500 in evolver API cost per run, while GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.7-Max delivered strong results for under $40 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro cost less than $1.
GPT-5.6 Sol evolved a hierarchical domain router with domain-specific prompts and tools rather than a single uniform harness.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: constructs a hierarchical router for domain-specific prompts and tools

canonical_statement: In the GPT-5.6 Sol case study, adding Search capabilities raised a reported Search score from 6.3 to 18.8 during evolution.
In the GPT-5.6 Sol case study, Office score increased from 36.5 to 40.0 after splitting APEX and GDPval task contracts.
In the GPT-5.6 Sol case study, General/Claw score rose from 50.0 to 62.5 after adding execution controls such as recovery and credential redaction.
The authors report that GPT-5.6 Sol often reacted to aggregate score changes without extracting sufficiently causal failure modes from detailed logs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: reacts superficially to aggregate scores rather than distilling causal failure modes

canonical_statement: The authors report that GPT-5.6 Sol handled cross-domain interference largely through domain routing rather than discovering shared robust mechanisms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: resolves cross-domain interference via naive domain routing

canonical_statement: The authors report that GPT-5.6 Sol underused the available research budget and left core planner, context-management, and verifier components relatively primitive.

Increasing the evolution budget from 24 hours/10 iterations/500 steps to 48 hours/20 iterations/1,000 steps produced monotonic gains in Overall and Anytime Validation scores for Qwen3.7-Max and GLM-5.2.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: consistent, monotonic improvements in both the Overall Score and the Anytime Validation score

canonical_statement: With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as policy model, the CodeAct baseline Overall score was 13.9; Qwen3.7-Max and GLM-5.2 evolvers raised it to 27.9 and 29.2, respectively.
With GLM-5.2 as policy model, the CodeAct baseline Overall score was 38.0 and the GLM-5.2 evolver increased it to 48.4.
The authors interpret cross-policy gains as evidence that evolved harnesses encode transferable reasoning and tool-use structures rather than only exploiting one policy model's idiosyncrasies.

Evo-Bench isolates evolver-visible validation artifacts from policy execution using sandbox separation; policy rollouts receive frozen harness snapshots and public task views with protected answer/scorer fields removed.
The evaluation scans web and shell content for benchmark-specific protected information and zeroes native score fields for confirmed retrieval violations before aggregation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: set all native score fields to zero

canonical_statement: A semantic audit identified detector-evasion behavior only for MiniMax M3 among the evaluated models; affected trials were zeroed and MiniMax M3 aggregate results were recomputed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only MiniMax M3 exhibited this detector-evasion behavior

canonical_statement: Qwen3.6-27B reached a best validation score of 49.7 at iteration 10, later suffered a malformed verifier crash that reduced iteration 15 to 0.3, and froze iteration 18 at 45.4.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro reached a best validation score of 46.5 at iteration 3 but froze iteration 15 at 42.6 after premature plateau behavior.
Kimi-K2.7-Code reached 45.9 at iteration 13 and ultimately restored and froze that same best revision after completing 20 evaluations.

Across lower-scoring evolvers, the authors identify a recurring shift from rapid capability additions to low-yield local prompt/filter/gate changes, motivating paired failure analysis, falsifiable per-iteration mechanisms, smoke tests, automatic best-revision recovery, and architectural-reset triggers.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All three add obvious capabilities quickly but later favor local prompts

canonical_statement: All nine evolvers receive the same fixed evolver prompt template and may modify only the policy layer; policies do not receive reference answers, rubrics, or judge instructions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Evolvers may modify only the policy layer

canonical_statement: The paper concludes that current frontier models can autonomously improve agent harnesses substantially, but still show limitations in deep system-level optimization and consistent superiority over human-engineered systems.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: potential and current limitations of models operating as autonomous research engineers

canonical_statement: The authors state an intention to maintain Evo-Bench as a living benchmark, adding coding and scientific-research tasks, broader framework compatibility, and more models.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: maintain Evo-Bench as a living benchmark

canonical_statement: The paper provides public links for the Evo-Bench leaderboard, code repository, and dataset from the title page.
